warnings.description: North Sea coast from Staithes to Whitby including tidal River Esk
warnings.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain. 
Coastal conditions are expected to improve and no flooding is expected.   
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.   
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger. Stay away from floodwater - it contains hidden dangers such as open manhole covers, sewage and chemicals.

warnings.label: Hunstanton coast in Norfolk
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 06:30am to 10:30am on Tuesday 29th September 2026. 
Areas most at risk are around Hunstanton seafront. Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at King's Lynn of 4.58mAODN at 08:30am on 29 September 2026, Wind Force 5, Easterly. The current series of high spring tides has now reached its peak and will fall away over the next few days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded around high tide. 
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on 29 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The tidal River Waveney from Ellingham to Breydon Water
warnings.description: The tidal River Waveney from Ellingham to Breydon Water
warnings.message:
High river levels today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible today, Monday 28th September. 
We expect to see high water levels at Beccles Quay. River levels will remain high over the next couple of days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water . Avoid using low lying footpaths which may be flooded. 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 29 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The tidal Deben estuary
warnings.message:
High tides this afternoon may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 12:30pm and 2:30pm today, Monday 28th September. 
Tide levels will be high around the boat yard in Felixstowe Ferry hamlet at the end of Ferry Road, and along riverside areas in Woodbridge and Waldringfield, as well as in surrounding marshland. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Harwich of 2.56mAODN at 1:30pm, on Monday 28th September, which is 0.5m above tide tables, Wind Force 3, North Easterly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 29 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Tidal areas of Shoreham Harbour
warnings.message:
High tides on Monday may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible for 1 hour either side of Monday afternoon's tide at 13:00 on 28/09/2026.. 
The weather increases tide table values by 0.5 m. Total forecast tide is 6.90 metres Chart Datum (3.63 mAOD) at Shoreham. Light North Easterly Force 3 wind. The tide will come close to the top of walls and slipways in Shoreham Town. Minor impact flooding will affect Sussex Yacht Club. Riverbank houseboats will be raised higher than normal, making access to them temporarily more difficult. Tuesday's tide at 01:15 29/09/2026 is forecast to be 16 cm lower (3.47 mAOD).  Flood impacts should reduce‚ but could return on Tuesday afternoon's tide at 13:30 29/09/2026. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 6:00PM on 28 September 2026 or as the situation changes.
